correctness.rationale: Let Y=Bl_p X_a. The original 107-page author-hosted primary shows H²(X_a,Z)=0, H²(Y,Z)=Z[E], c1(TY)=-2[E], E=P² with normal O(-1). A biholomorphism F:Y->Y′ preserves c1, hence sends the target exceptional divisor back to an effective divisor D in cohomology class [E]. If D and E are distinct irreducible divisors, the canonical holomorphic section of O(D) restricts to a nonzero section of O(D)|E; by H²(E,Z)=Z and [D]=[E], this line bundle is O_{P²}(-1), with no sections. Therefore D=E. The map descends holomorphically across contractions of E and E′ (holomorphic rigidity/blow-down universal property) to g:X_a->X_{a′}, g(p)=q, with inverse descending similarly. Conversely such a pointed base isomorphism lifts. For fixed a the source proves Aut(X_a)=C* (indeed not merely connected component); its orbits in a real 6-manifold are real dimension at most 2, hence measure zero and cannot cover X_a with countably many orbits. The uncountable orbit quotient classifies one-point blow-ups, not arbitrary multipoint cases or deformation equivalence.
